hypotheses.claim: For FRANK recurrence control, a deterministic post-hoc readout over a frozen short trajectory can reduce transient false-halt decisions compared with a one-state threshold controller without shaping the trajectory itself.
hypotheses.prediction: On matched frozen H1 and later target-4B recurrence traces, the post-hoc baseline will improve the false-halt/extra-compute frontier for at least one nontrivial task family.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Windowing merely delays valid halts and adds compute; the existing single-state controller equals or dominates it once thresholds are calibrated.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched trace evaluation where the post-hoc baseline never improves false-halt rate at equal or lower total recurrence cost and consistently increases latency/overshoot.

hypotheses.claim: A learned halting gate should not become FRANK's default recurrence controller unless it beats simple frozen-trajectory readouts and fixed-depth baselines under matched quality, latency and intervention robustness.
hypotheses.prediction: Some learned gates will fail to dominate simple baselines because trajectory formation and readout quality are separable failure sources.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: FRANK-specific signals are sufficiently different from looped-transformer experiments that an end-to-end learned gate consistently dominates simple readouts.
hypotheses.falsifier: Repeated H1 and target-4B trials showing a learned gate Pareto-dominates fixed-depth, single-step and post-hoc baselines across task families and OOD conditions.

hypotheses.claim: For high-risk correction decisions made by a small local model, FRANK should prefer an independent stronger verifier/peer when available rather than trusting weak self-verification as the sole stop/correct signal.
hypotheses.prediction: Verifier-backed correction will improve error localization or calibration on at least some difficult tasks, particularly when the 4B's own verifier is weak.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The additional verifier adds latency/cost/dependency without material accuracy gain after local fine-tuning and recurrence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target-4B experiments where local self-verification matches or exceeds strong-peer verification at lower cost across safety-relevant and reasoning tasks.

hypotheses.claim: FRANK's external-effect authority should remain host-rooted and handle/capability based; cognitive state, model text, recurrence receipts and diagnostic records must remain descriptive and unable to mint bearer authority.
hypotheses.prediction: A typed handle/import boundary plus Linux sandbox restrictions can preserve expressibility while making authority provenance independently testable.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The extra capability/host boundary is redundant because process sandboxing alone is sufficient for all FRANK effect safety requirements.
hypotheses.falsifier: A simpler architecture demonstrates equivalent least-authority, delegation, revocation, replay and confused-deputy resistance under the same adversarial test suite.

hypotheses.claim: Qwen3.5-4B is a materially stronger current candidate for the local Clay-native 4B because it is an official 4B vision-language model with a hybrid recurrent/attention architecture, but runtime/backend maturity must be treated as a moving target rather than assumed.
hypotheses.prediction: A pinned Linux runtime build will execute the target 4B with acceptable text/vision correctness and resource cost, but some runtime versions/backends will regress or expose unsupported paths.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Another Qwen-class 4B/runtime pairing is more stable or efficient for the owner hardware and FRANK workload despite weaker nominal feature fit.
hypotheses.falsifier: Pinned owner-host benchmarks showing Qwen3.5-4B materially loses on latency/RAM/vision/tool workload or backend reliability versus another candidate.

hypotheses.claim: Recurrence readout quality and ActiveAssembly conflict allocation interact: a controller can appear stalled or uncertain because its active slice is budget-starved, so recurrence policy must not be optimized independently of Assembly selection quality.
hypotheses.prediction: Under conflict-dense traces, at least part of apparent recurrence pressure disappears when Assembly allocation improves at fixed model and recurrence policy.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Assembly composition has negligible effect on recurrence dynamics once the core state summary is present.
hypotheses.falsifier: Factorial Assembly-policy x recurrence-policy experiments show no meaningful interaction on task outcome, residual pressure, correction time or compute.

next_discriminator: Run matched frozen H1 trajectories through existing single-state controller, new post-hoc trajectory baseline and later a learned-gate candidate; compare false halt, extra recurrence count, routing/rollback correctness, task outcome and latency.
